plain: A school plan for a student with a disability who does not need special education. It gives accommodations, such as more time on tests.
pro: Plan under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. A 504 plan alone does not bring an IDEA transition plan, but it is enough proof for Pre-ETS.

plain: Area Agency on Aging. A local agency that helps older adults and family caregivers age 55 and older.
pro: Area Agency on Aging; runs Older Americans Act programs, including the National Family Caregiver Support Program, through DHSS. In this region: SeniorAge, Region X AAA, Care Connection for Aging Services, and Aging Best.

plain: Access and Accommodation Resources. The disability office at Ozarks Technical Community College.
pro: OTC Access & Accommodation Resources (formerly Disability Support Services); arranges Section 504 and ADA accommodations.

plain: Applied Behavior Analysis. A therapy that teaches skills and helps change behavior.
pro: Applied Behavior Analysis; a Brain Injury Waiver service. MO HealthNet lists ABA for autism under age 21 only.

plain: A special savings account for a person whose disability started before a set age. Money in it does not count against most benefits, up to set limits.
pro: Achieving a Better Life Experience account (26 USC 529A). From 2026, onset must be before age 46. 2026 contribution limit $20,000. SSI excludes the first $100,000.

plain: Americans with Disabilities Act. A federal law that bans disability discrimination.
pro: Americans with Disabilities Act. Title II requires ADA complementary paratransit (49 CFR 37 Subpart F).

plain: Adult Day Care Waiver. It pays for a licensed adult day care center for adults age 18 to 62 when they start.
pro: DSDS Adult Day Care Waiver; first authorization ages 18 to 62; nursing facility level of care; up to 10 hours a day, 5 days a week.

plain: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.
pro: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder.

plain: Aged and Disabled Waiver. Home services for adults age 63 and older, including respite.
pro: DSDS Aged and Disabled Waiver; age 63 or over; homemaker, chore, respite, home delivered meals, adult day care.

plain: The letter DHSS sends when it denies, cuts, or stops home care. The appeal clock starts on its mail date.
pro: DSDS form HCBS-12. Appeal within 10 calendar days of the mail date to keep services; 90 calendar days to appeal a denial (HCBS Manual 6.00).

plain: Adjusted gross income. The income number on a federal tax return.
pro: Adjusted gross income; used for the MoAT TAP income test.

plain: Assisted living facility.
pro: Assisted living facility; DSDS can authorize state plan personal care there for a Medicaid resident whose needs exceed the facility's basic duties.

plain: Area median income. The middle income for an area. Housing programs use a percent of it as a limit.
pro: Area median income; for example DMH RAP (under 50% AMI) and Missouri 811 (30% AMI or below).

plain: Advanced practice nurse.
pro: Advanced practice nurse; may order DME with a collaborative practice agreement that allows it.

plain: Adult Protective Services. The state office that checks on adults who may be unsafe. Hotline: 1-800-392-0210.
pro: DHSS DSDS Adult Protective Services; eligible adult is 18 to 59 with a disability, or 60 and over.

plain: A national respite network. Its map shows no Missouri respite coalition.
pro: ARCH National Respite Network; its State Respite Coalition and Lifespan Respite map had no Missouri entry (checked 26 Oct 2026).

plain: Assistive technology. Devices or tools that help a person with a disability do things.
pro: Assistive technology (devices and services).

plain: Assistive Technology Professional. A certified expert in complex equipment such as power wheelchairs.
pro: RESNA-certified Assistive Technology Professional; MO HealthNet complex rehab technology suppliers must employ one (since 1 Aug 2025).

plain: Brain Injury Waiver. Services for adults age 21 to 65 with a traumatic brain injury.
pro: DHSS Brain Injury Waiver; ages 21 to 65; fee-for-service MO HealthNet; nursing home LOC; $32,000 a year cap.

plain: Bureau of Special Health Care Needs. The DHSS office for the Medically Complex Adult Waiver.
pro: DHSS Bureau of Special Health Care Needs; (800) 451-0669 in the MFAW manual grievance text.

plain: Client Assistance Program. Free help with problems with VR. Call 800-392-8667.
pro: Client Assistance Program at Missouri Protection and Advocacy Services, 800-392-8667.

plain: Consumer Directed Services. The person hires and directs their own home care worker.
pro: Consumer Directed Services, MO HealthNet state plan Personal Care Assistance (HCBS Manual 3.25). The attendant cannot be the spouse or legal guardian.

plain: Code of Federal Regulations. The book of federal agency rules.
pro: Code of Federal Regulations.

plain: Children's Health Insurance Program.
pro: Children's Health Insurance Program; some premium CHIP ME codes are not eligible for NEMT.

plain: Center for Independent Living. A local nonprofit run by and for people with disabilities. Some build ramps and lend equipment.
pro: Center for Independent Living. In this region: empower: abilities, The Independent Living Center (Joplin), On My Own, Ozark Independent Living, West-Central Independent Living Solutions. None serves Laclede County.

plain: Certificate of Medical Necessity. A form that shows why the person needs the equipment.
pro: MO HealthNet DME Certificate of Medical Necessity; approved for 6 months from the prescription date, 12 months for wheelchair codes K0001, K0002, K0003, K0006.

plain: Other help the person can use first, such as insurance or Medicaid. VR uses these before it pays.
pro: Benefits such as insurance, Medicaid, or Pell grants that MVR must use before paying for a service.

plain: A regular job in the community, at regular pay, alongside people without disabilities.
pro: Employment at or above minimum wage in an integrated setting; 'the first and preferred outcome' under RSMo 209.700.

plain: Cooperative Work Experience Program. A paid job during high school that earns credit.
pro: Cooperative Work Experience Program run by a school district with MVR; age 16 and older, IEP, VR eligible with an IPE.

plain: Community rehabilitation program. A provider that VR pays to help people find and keep jobs.
pro: Community rehabilitation program; a VR-contracted employment provider.

plain: Code of State Regulations. The book of Missouri agency rules.
pro: Missouri Code of State Regulations.

plain: Community Support Waiver. A DD waiver for people who live in the community.
pro: DMH DD Community Support Waiver; new enrollment wait-listed since 15 Oct 2026.

plain: City Utilities of Springfield. It runs the city bus and Access Express.
pro: City Utilities of Springfield, Transit Services (CU Transit).

plain: The driver picks you up and drops you off at the curb. The driver does not come inside.
pro: Basic Access Express service mode; origin-to-destination help is available on request.

plain: The person's MO HealthNet ID number.
pro: MO HealthNet participant identification number.

plain: Developmental disability. A lifelong disability that starts in childhood, such as intellectual disability, autism, or cerebral palsy.
pro: Developmental disability as defined for DMH eligibility (RSMo 630.005); onset before age 22.

plain: Division of Developmental Disabilities. The part of DMH that runs DD services.
pro: DMH Division of Developmental Disabilities.

plain: Missouri Department of Elementary and Secondary Education. It oversees schools and runs Missouri VR.
pro: Department of Elementary and Secondary Education; Office of Special Education and Office of Adult Learning and Rehabilitation Services.

plain: Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services. It runs in-home care and several waivers.
pro: Department of Health and Senior Services; DSDS, SHCN, and the Bureau of Long-Term Services and Supports.

plain: Durable medical equipment. Medical items such as wheelchairs, walkers, hospital beds, and lifts.
pro: Durable medical equipment under the MO HealthNet DME Manual (07/06/2026).

plain: Missouri Department of Mental Health. It runs DD services and mental health services.
pro: Department of Mental Health, including the Division of Developmental Disabilities and the Housing Unit.

plain: Division of Senior and Disability Services. The part of DHSS that runs in-home care.
pro: DHSS Division of Senior and Disability Services; HCBS Call Center 866-835-3505.

plain: Direct support professional. A paid worker who helps a person with a disability.
pro: Direct support professional.

plain: Missouri Department of Social Services. It runs MO HealthNet.
pro: Department of Social Services, including the Family Support Division and the MO HealthNet Division.

plain: Employer-Based Transition Training. A final school year spent learning at a business. None was found in Southwest Missouri.
pro: Employer-Based Transition Training (including Project SEARCH); ages 18 to 21 in the final year of school eligibility.

plain: The Medicaid health benefit for people under 21. In Missouri it is called HCY.
pro: Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic and Treatment; Missouri's program is Healthy Children and Youth (HCY).

plain: Electronic visit verification. A system that records when the home care worker starts and ends each visit.
pro: Electronic Visit Verification; CDS participants must monitor it.

plain: A way for a doctor to ask MO HealthNet to pay for an item it does not usually cover.
pro: MO HealthNet Exceptions process (13 CSR 70-2.100; Exceptions Manual); initiated by the treating prescriber; high bar (life-sustaining, or prevents a higher level of care).

plain: Free appropriate public education. The right to free special education until a regular diploma or age 21.
pro: Free appropriate public education under IDEA; ends at a regular diploma or age 21 (State Plan Regulation IV).

plain: Frequently asked questions.
pro: Frequently asked questions.

plain: Regular MO HealthNet, where the state pays providers directly. It is not a managed care health plan.
pro: MO HealthNet fee-for-service, as opposed to a MO HealthNet managed care plan; required for MCAW and BIW.

plain: Federal fiscal year. It runs from 1 October to 30 September.
pro: Federal fiscal year (1 Oct to 30 Sep).

plain: Fair Labor Standards Act. A federal wage law. Section 14(c) allows pay below minimum wage in some jobs.
pro: Fair Labor Standards Act; section 14(c) subminimum wage certificates remain available in 2026.

plain: Family Support Division. The state office that decides MO HealthNet applications.
pro: DSS Family Support Division.

plain: Fiscal year. A 12-month budget year.
pro: Fiscal year.

plain: Governor's Council on Disability.
pro: Missouri Governor's Council on Disability.

plain: Housing Authority of the City of Springfield.
pro: Housing Authority of the City of Springfield, PHA code MO058.

plain: House Bill. A bill in the Missouri House.
pro: House Bill.

plain: A MO HealthNet group for people who need home care. FSD decides it.
pro: Home and Community Based Medicaid; DSDS sends people who appear eligible to FSD first.

plain: Home and community based services. Care at home or in the community instead of a nursing home.
pro: Home and community based services.

plain: The DHSS referral form for in-home care.
pro: DSDS referral form; email to HCBSCallCenterReferrals@health.mo.gov.

plain: Housing Choice Voucher, also called Section 8. It helps pay rent to a private landlord.
pro: HUD Housing Choice Voucher program, run by local public housing agencies.

plain: Healthy Children and Youth. MO HealthNet's extra health benefit for people under 21.
pro: Healthy Children and Youth, Missouri's EPSDT program; 'A medically necessary item or service that is normally non-covered ... may be covered for participants ages 20 and under.'

plain: High School Equivalency. It is not a regular diploma.
pro: High School Equivalency certificate; does not end FAPE under 21.

plain: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
pro: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

plain: A program that gives equipment to people who are DeafBlind.
pro: National DeafBlind equipment distribution program, listed by MoAT; rules not checked.

plain: A code system for medical diagnoses.
pro: International Classification of Diseases codes.

plain: Information Commons East, a building on the OTC Springfield campus.
pro: Information Commons East (OTC Springfield campus); AAR is in Room ICE 110.

plain: A care facility for people with intellectual disabilities. Some waivers require a need for this level of care.
pro: Intermediate Care Facility for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities; ICF-IID level of care requires a developmental disability as defined in 42 CFR 435.1010.

plain: Identification, such as a state ID card or driver license.
pro: Identification document.

plain: Intellectual and developmental disabilities.
pro: Intellectual and developmental disabilities.

plain: Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. The federal special education law.
pro: Individuals with Disabilities Education Act, Part B; Missouri implements it through the State Plan for Special Education.

plain: Individualized Education Program. The written special education plan for a student.
pro: Individualized Education Program under IDEA.

plain: Independent Living Waiver. More self-directed care hours for adults with physical disabilities.
pro: DSDS Independent Living Waiver; ages 18 to 64 at first enrollment; physical disability; must self-direct CDS.

plain: The test DHSS uses at the home visit to score care needs.
pro: interRAI Home Care assessment tool with Missouri changes; 18 points or more meets nursing facility level of care.

plain: Individualized Plan for Employment. The written job plan made with VR.
pro: Individualized Plan for Employment; due within 90 days of VR eligibility and before exit for students.

plain: Internal Revenue Service.
pro: Internal Revenue Service; NEMT mileage is paid at no less than the IRS medical mileage rate.

plain: Individualized Supported Living. A DD waiver home service.
pro: Individualized Supported Living (DD waiver residential service); ISL participants cannot also get DSDS state plan personal care.

plain: Local education agency. Usually the school district.
pro: Local education agency (school district).

plain: How much care a person needs. DHSS uses a score of 18 points as the line for home care.
pro: Nursing facility level of care for DSDS HCBS: 'A score of 18 or higher qualifies for LOC and HCBS'. DD waivers and MCAW use ICF-IID level of care.

plain: Legal Information Institute. A free website with copies of laws.
pro: Cornell Legal Information Institute (secondary copies of regulations).

plain: Least restrictive environment. Students learn with peers without disabilities as much as possible.
pro: Least restrictive environment under IDEA.

plain: Long-term services and supports.
pro: Long-term services and supports; the DHSS Bureau of LTSS runs the Brain Injury Waiver.

plain: A housing voucher set aside for adults with disabilities under age 62.
pro: HUD Mainstream voucher for non-elderly persons with disabilities; HACS 23, Jasper County PHA 100, OACAC none (HUD, 2023).

plain: A health plan that manages MO HealthNet care for its members. Its name is on the member's card.
pro: MO HealthNet managed care health plan; members use the plan for NEMT and DME, and some are not eligible for certain DSDS HCBS.

plain: Medically Complex Adult Waiver. Private duty nursing at home for adults 21 and older.
pro: DHSS SHCN Medically Complex Adult Waiver (formerly MFAW); requires prior HCY PDN or documented PDN need before 21.

plain: Medicaid eligibility code. It shows which MO HealthNet group the person is in.
pro: Medicaid Eligibility code; determines access to HCBS, NEMT, and waivers.

plain: A nonprofit job services provider.
pro: Employment provider listed on the DMH Employment Service Providers map.

plain: Medically Fragile Adult Waiver. The old name of the Medically Complex Adult Waiver.
pro: Medically Fragile Adult Waiver; name still used in the MO HealthNet provider manual (2026/03).

plain: MO HealthNet Division. The part of DSS that runs Missouri Medicaid.
pro: DSS MO HealthNet Division; Constituent Services (800) 392-2161.

plain: Missouri Housing Development Commission. It runs Missouri 811.
pro: Missouri Housing Development Commission.

plain: A special trust for income. DHSS lists it as an exception to the spenddown rule for home care. Ask FSD.
pro: Qualified income trust; HCBS Manual 4.05 lists it (form IM-54A) as an exception to the rule that spenddown cases are not processed until met.

plain: Missouri Medicaid Audit and Compliance. It enrolls and checks MO HealthNet providers.
pro: Missouri Medicaid Audit and Compliance Unit; posted the 1 Aug 2026 DME and CDS/Personal Care enrollment moratoria.

plain: Missouri's Medicaid program. It pays for health care and many disability services.
pro: Missouri Medicaid, administered by DSS (FSD for eligibility, MHD for coverage).

plain: The federal code for Missouri Vocational Rehabilitation.
pro: RSA designation for Missouri Vocational Rehabilitation (general agency).

plain: A DD waiver for children under 18. It is also called the Lopez waiver.
pro: Missouri Children with Developmental Disabilities waiver (Sarah Jian Lopez Waiver); under 18; not affected by the 15 Oct 2026 wait list memo.

plain: A pause. Here it means Missouri is not enrolling new providers for a time.
pro: Six-month temporary moratorium on new DME and CDS/Personal Care provider enrollments from 1 Aug 2026, may extend in 6-month steps up to 1 year.

plain: Missouri State University, in Springfield.
pro: Missouri State University.

plain: MTM Health. The company that schedules MO HealthNet rides.
pro: MTM Health, the statewide MO HealthNet NEMT broker named in the 2026 NEMT Manual.

plain: University of Missouri.
pro: University of Missouri (College of Education runs Pre-ETS under contract with MVR).

plain: Missouri Vocational Rehabilitation. The state job help program for people with disabilities.
pro: DESE Missouri Vocational Rehabilitation; order of selection with Categories II and III closed since 9 Dec 2024.

plain: National Core Indicators. A national survey of disability services.
pro: National Core Indicators, Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities; State of the Workforce 2024 report.

plain: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation. Free MO HealthNet rides to covered medical visits.
pro: MO HealthNet Non-Emergency Medical Transportation through the broker MTM Health.

plain: Notice of Funding Availability. A call for funding applications.
pro: Notice of Funding Availability.

plain: Missouri Office of Administration.
pro: Missouri Office of Administration (state budget documents).

plain: Ozarks Area Community Action Corporation. It runs housing vouchers outside Springfield city limits.
pro: Ozarks Area Community Action Corporation, PHA code MO216.

plain: OATS Transit. A nonprofit that runs public van rides in rural Missouri.
pro: OATS Transit, nonprofit rural public transit in 87 Missouri counties.

plain: The doctor or nurse who orders the equipment.
pro: Ordering, prescribing, or referring provider; must be actively enrolled with MHD or the DME claim is denied.

plain: The VR wait list rule. When money is short, VR serves people with the most serious disabilities first.
pro: VR priority system (34 CFR 361.36). Missouri: Category I open; Categories II and III closed since 9 Dec 2024.

plain: Occupational therapy.
pro: Occupational therapy.

plain: Ozarks Technical Community College.
pro: Ozarks Technical Community College.

plain: Prior authorization. Approval MO HealthNet must give before it pays for some items.
pro: Prior authorization; for DME it expires 3 months after approval unless stated.

plain: Van rides for people who cannot use the regular bus because of a disability.
pro: ADA complementary paratransit (49 CFR 37 Subpart F); in Springfield, CU Access Express.

plain: Personal care attendant. A helper who rides along. On Access Express, the attendant rides free.
pro: Personal care attendant.

plain: Person-centered service plan. The DD plan that lists the person's services.
pro: Person-Centered Service Plan (DD waiver).

plain: A type of computer file for documents.
pro: Portable Document Format.

plain: Private duty nursing. A nurse who gives ongoing care in the home.
pro: Private duty nursing; under HCY for under 21; for 21 and older only through MCAW.

plain: Partnership for Hope. A DD waiver with a lower yearly cap.
pro: Partnership for Hope DD waiver; new enrollment wait-listed since 15 Oct 2026; respite is not a PfH service.

plain: Public housing agency. A local agency that runs housing vouchers and public housing.
pro: Public housing agency. HUD codes in this data: MO058 (HACS), MO215 (Jasper County PHA), MO216 (OACAC).

plain: Prioritization of Need. A score from 1 to 5 that sets a person's place on the DD waiver wait list.
pro: Prioritization of Need (also called Priority of Need), 1 to 5; PON 5 means verified emergency criteria (9 CSR 45-2.017).

plain: Pre-Employment Transition Services. Free job training for students with disabilities, ages 14 to 21.
pro: Pre-Employment Transition Services (Rehabilitation Act); five required activities; not subject to the order of selection for potentially eligible students.

plain: Permission to use a service while the agency is still deciding. Access Express gives it after 21 days with no decision.
pro: ADA paratransit rule: if no decision within 21 days of a complete application, the applicant is treated as eligible until a decision (49 CFR 37.125(c)).

plain: A letter the school must send before it changes a student's services, including a regular diploma.
pro: IDEA prior written notice; graduation with a regular diploma is a change in placement that requires it (Regulation IV).

plain: A final school year program at a business for students with intellectual disabilities. None was found in Southwest Missouri.
pro: Employer-based transition model (EBTT) with school, MVR, CRP, long-term support provider, and host business partners.

plain: Project Rental Assistance. Rent help tied to certain apartments.
pro: HUD Section 811 Project Rental Assistance.

plain: Physical therapy.
pro: Physical therapy.

plain: Program year.
pro: Program year (VR state plan).

plain: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary. A program that helps pay Medicare costs.
pro: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary; ME code 55 (QMB only) is not eligible for NEMT.

plain: Rental Assistance Program. One-time DMH rent help for people in mental health services. Closed through January 2027.
pro: DMH Housing Unit Rental Assistance Program.

plain: Residential care facility.
pro: Residential care facility; DSDS can authorize state plan personal care there for Medicaid residents.

plain: A standard high school diploma. It ends special education services.
pro: Regular high school diploma; ends FAPE. A certificate of attendance or HSE does not.

plain: A group that certifies experts in assistive technology.
pro: Professional society that certifies Assistive Technology Professionals (ATP).

plain: Short-term care that gives the main caregiver a break.
pro: Respite care; in this region through DD waivers (not PfH), SB40 boards, AAA Family Caregiver Support, and ADW (63 and older).

plain: Registered nurse.
pro: Registered nurse.

plain: Rehabilitation Services Administration. The federal office over VR.
pro: U.S. Department of Education Rehabilitation Services Administration.

plain: Rehabilitation Services for the Blind. Job and transition help for people who are blind or have low vision.
pro: DSS Family Support Division, Rehabilitation Services for the Blind; 1-800-592-6004.

plain: Revised Statutes of Missouri. The state laws.
pro: Revised Statutes of Missouri.

plain: A county board that uses local tax money for DD services.
pro: County developmental disability board under RSMo 205.968 to 205.972.

plain: A federal rule. Youth age 24 and under must take VR steps before a job that pays below minimum wage.
pro: Rehabilitation Act section 511: no subminimum wage employment while a student; for age 24 and under, Pre-ETS and transition documentation, MVR career counseling and information and referral, and MVR documentation first.

plain: To hire, train, and supervise your own care worker.
pro: CDS requirement: supervise the attendant, verify wages and time, monitor EVV, report changes.

plain: Structured Family Caregiving Waiver. It can pay a live-in caregiver for an adult with dementia.
pro: DSDS Structured Family Caregiving Waiver; age 21 and older with Alzheimer's or related dementia; caregiver may be family or legal guardian.

plain: State fiscal year.
pro: State fiscal year.

plain: Special Health Care Needs. The DHSS office for the Medically Complex Adult Waiver. Phone 573-751-6246.
pro: DHSS Special Health Care Needs.

plain: A workplace for people with disabilities, separate from regular jobs. Pay can be below minimum wage.
pro: DESE-certified extended employment sheltered workshop (RSMo 178.900 to 178.931).

plain: Summary of Performance. A school report given when the student leaves school.
pro: Summary of Performance, required at exit by regular diploma or age 21 (Regulation III).

plain: An amount of medical bills a person must pay or owe each month before MO HealthNet pays.
pro: MO HealthNet spend down: countable income above the non-spend-down limit; DSDS does not process HCBS referrals until it is met.

plain: Springfield Public Schools.
pro: Springfield R-XII School District.

plain: Social Security Administration.
pro: Social Security Administration.

plain: Social Security Disability Insurance. Monthly money based on a work record.
pro: Social Security Disability Insurance (title II).

plain: Supplemental Security Income. Monthly money for people with a disability and low income.
pro: Supplemental Security Income (title XVI).

plain: A real job with help from a job coach.
pro: Supported employment; funded by MVR to case closure, then by a long-term funder such as a DD waiver.

plain: Telecommunications Access Program. Adapted phones (TAP-T) and computer tools (TAP-I) from MoAT.
pro: MoAT Telecommunications Access Program: TAP-T (telephone) and TAP-I (internet).

plain: The part of TAP that gives adapted computer tools.
pro: TAP Internet: adaptive input and output; no computers or speech generating devices.

plain: The part of TAP that gives adapted phones.
pro: TAP Telephone: text, carry-over, amplified, Braille, hands-free, and photo phones.

plain: Traumatic brain injury. A brain injury caused by an outside force.
pro: Traumatic brain injury.

plain: College programs for students with intellectual disabilities at other Missouri universities.
pro: UCM THRIVE, MU PAWS, UMSL Succeed (named in a 2024 governor's proclamation).

plain: School help to plan for adult life: work, more school, and daily living.
pro: IDEA postsecondary transition services in the IEP, based on age-appropriate transition assessments.

plain: University of Central Missouri.
pro: University of Central Missouri.

plain: University of Missouri St. Louis.
pro: University of Missouri St. Louis.

plain: U.S. Department of Agriculture. It has home repair loans and grants for some rural homeowners.
pro: USDA Rural Development; Section 504 Home Repair loans and grants (amounts not verified).

plain: Vocational Rehabilitation. The state program that helps people with disabilities get and keep jobs.
pro: Vocational Rehabilitation; in Missouri, MVR (DESE) and RSB (DSS).

plain: The written agreement between VR and the state school agency about transition.
pro: VR and State Educational Agency Transition Agreement FY26, signed 4 Nov 2025.

plain: A Medicaid program that pays for services at home and in the community.
pro: Medicaid home and community based services waiver; a person may be in only one HCBS waiver at a time.

plain: Work Experience Coordinator. The teacher who runs COOP at a high school.
pro: Certified special education teacher approved as Work Experience Coordinator.

plain: West-Central Independent Living Solutions. The independent living center for Henry County.
pro: West-Central Independent Living Solutions, Sedalia.

plain: The 5-digit postal code. In Greene County, the ZIP code decides which VR office serves you.
pro: Postal code; MVR splits Greene County between Springfield North and South by ZIP code.
